entries.displayName: RS-BA1 v2 — direct to radio LAN port

stationTarget.label: Radio's IP address on the Station's LAN
stationTarget.why: This is where the Station sends traffic after it comes out of the tunnel. The Station is already on the same LAN as your radio, so this is the radio's ordinary local address -- not a Tailscale address, and not your public IP.
stationTarget.howToFind: On the radio: MENU -> SET -> Network -> IP Address. Set a fixed address rather than DHCP; if the radio's lease changes, these rules point at nothing.
stationTarget.ifWrong: The rules will bind normally and the Status column will read 'Listening'. Nothing will report an error. Remote Utility will simply fail to connect, or hang at the login step.

clientNotes: Remote Utility -> Server List: address 127.0.0.1, control port 50001
Leave 'Server Setting' completely blank on the client side
The Radio List fills itself in on the first successful connect
stationNotes: No station-side software required -- radio serves RS-BA1 directly
radioNotes: Set a fixed LAN IP on the radio (do not rely on DHCP)
Register a Network User with a password in the radio's Network menu

stationTarget.label: RS-BA1 Server PC address
stationTarget.why: The Remote Utility server runs on this PC. If it's the same machine as RWK Station, use 127.0.0.1. If it's a different PC on the Station's LAN, use that PC's LAN address.
stationTarget.howToFind: If the server is on the Station PC itself: 127.0.0.1. Otherwise: run ipconfig on the server PC and use its IPv4 address.
stationTarget.ifWrong: Remote Utility will fail to connect with no useful diagnostic. The rules will show 'Listening' normally.

clientNotes: Remote Utility -> Server List: address 127.0.0.1, control port 50001
Leave 'Server Setting' completely blank on the client side
The Remote Utility server must be RUNNING on the station PC (it is a foreground program)
stationNotes: RS-BA1 Remote Utility Server must be running on the station PC
The server is a foreground program, not a Windows service
radioNotes: Radio must be connected to the server PC via USB or CI-V cable

stationTarget.label: Radio's IP address on the Station's LAN
stationTarget.why: wfview connects directly to the radio's LAN port using Icom's native protocol (same ports as RS-BA1).
stationTarget.howToFind: On the radio: MENU -> SET -> Network -> IP Address.
stationTarget.ifWrong: wfview will show 'Connecting...' and eventually time out.

clientNotes: wfview -> Radio Access = Network, hostname 127.0.0.1
Ports 50001/50002/50003, radio username and password as set in radio's Network menu
radioNotes: Set a fixed LAN IP on the radio
Register a Network User with a password

stationTarget.label: TS-890S IP address on the Station's LAN
stationTarget.why: The Station sends control and audio here after traffic leaves the tunnel. This is the radio's ordinary LAN address -- not a Tailscale address.
stationTarget.howToFind: On the radio: LAN menu -> IP Address. Set it manually; a DHCP lease change will silently break these rules.
stationTarget.ifWrong: Both rules bind and show 'Listening'. ARCP-890 fails to connect with no useful diagnostic.

clientNotes: Connection type: KNS (Directly to TS-890S)
IP address: 127.0.0.1
Leave the MAC address field BLANK -- use the Internet-mode configuration, not the LAN-mode one
Tick 'Use TS-890S Built-in VoIP'
radioNotes: KNS menu 1: KNS Operation (LAN Connector) = On (Internet)
KNS menu 3: Built-in VoIP = On
Modulation Source: DATA SEND audio input = LAN

stationTarget.label: ARHP host PC address
stationTarget.why: ARHP runs on a PC at the station connected to the radio via USB. If that PC is the RWK Station, use 127.0.0.1.
stationTarget.howToFind: If ARHP runs on the Station PC itself: 127.0.0.1. Otherwise run ipconfig on the ARHP PC.
stationTarget.ifWrong: ARCP will fail to connect to ARHP.

clientNotes: ARCP -> ARHP port number: 50000 (or whatever you set)
ARVP-10R -> connect to 127.0.0.1 port 33550
stationNotes: ARHP must be running on the station PC (foreground program)
Radio connected via USB or serial cable to the ARHP PC
Audio requires an analogue cable from radio's ACC 2 connector to the ARHP PC sound card

stationTarget.label: SCU-LAN10 IP address on the Station's LAN
stationTarget.why: The SCU-LAN10 interface has its own LAN address, separate from the radio. Traffic leaves the tunnel and goes to this address.
stationTarget.howToFind: Use the SCU-LAN10 Setting Tool to view or set the IP address. Set it to static.
stationTarget.ifWrong: All rules will show 'Listening' but the Remote Software will time out connecting.

clientNotes: SCU-LAN10 Remote Software -> IP Address: 127.0.0.1
Port settings must match (50000-50003 by default)
No public IP or dynamic DNS is needed -- RWK provides the tunnel
radioNotes: SCU-LAN10 must be connected to the radio and powered on
Set a static IP address via the SCU-LAN10 Setting Tool

stationTarget.label: K4 IP address on the Station's LAN
stationTarget.why: The K4 runs its own remote server. One TCP connection carries everything (commands, audio, panadapter).
stationTarget.howToFind: On the K4: CONFIG -> NETWORK. Note the IP address shown.
stationTarget.ifWrong: QK4 / Virtual K4 will fail to connect.

clientNotes: QK4 or Virtual K4 -> Server address: 127.0.0.1, port 9205
Only ONE rule is needed -- the K4 multiplexes everything on one TCP port
radioNotes: Enable Remote Server in the K4's CONFIG -> NETWORK menu
Set a static IP address

stationTarget.label: Radio-RRC IP address on the Station's LAN
stationTarget.why: The Radio-RRC box sits on the Station's LAN next to the radio. It has its own IP address.
stationTarget.howToFind: Check the Radio-RRC's web interface (default http://192.168.1.3) or use the RemoteRig IP scanning tool.
stationTarget.ifWrong: SIP registration will fail. The Control-RRC at your operating position will show 'No connection'.

clientNotes: IMPORTANT: These rules bind to 0.0.0.0, which means they are accessible from your LAN
Point your Control-RRC hardware at this PC's LAN IP address (not 127.0.0.1)
Ensure SIP ALG is disabled on your client-side router
radioNotes: Radio-RRC must have a static IP address on the Station's LAN

stationTarget.label: rigctld host address
stationTarget.why: rigctld listens on this address at the Station. Usually 127.0.0.1 if it runs on the Station PC.
stationTarget.howToFind: If rigctld runs on the Station PC: 127.0.0.1. If on another device, use that device's LAN IP.
stationTarget.ifWrong: CAT commands will time out.

clientNotes: Configure your logger/software to connect to 127.0.0.1:4532 for CAT
stationNotes: rigctld must be running on the Station PC

stationTarget.label: rotctld host address
stationTarget.why: rotctld listens on this address at the Station.
stationTarget.howToFind: If rotctld runs on the Station PC: 127.0.0.1.
stationTarget.ifWrong: Rotator commands will time out.

clientNotes: Configure your rotator control software to connect to 127.0.0.1:4533
stationNotes: rotctld must be running on the Station PC

stationTarget.label: RDP target address
stationTarget.why: Remote Desktop runs on the Station PC. Usually 127.0.0.1.
stationTarget.howToFind: 127.0.0.1 if connecting to the Station PC itself.
stationTarget.ifWrong: Remote Desktop will fail to connect.

clientNotes: Remote Desktop Connection -> Computer: 127.0.0.1
stationNotes: Remote Desktop must be enabled on the Station PC (Settings -> System -> Remote Desktop)

stationTarget.label: VNC server address
stationTarget.why: VNC server runs on the Station PC.
stationTarget.howToFind: 127.0.0.1 if VNC is on the Station PC.
stationTarget.ifWrong: VNC viewer will fail to connect.

clientNotes: VNC Viewer -> Server: 127.0.0.1:5900
stationNotes: VNC server must be running on the Station PC

stationTarget.label: PstRotator host address
stationTarget.why: PstRotator listens for TCP connections on this address.
stationTarget.howToFind: 127.0.0.1 if PstRotator runs on the Station PC.
stationTarget.ifWrong: Rotator control will time out.

clientNotes: Configure your rotator control to connect to 127.0.0.1:12000
stationNotes: PstRotator must be running with TCP server enabled

stationTarget.label: Antenna Genius IP address on the Station's LAN
stationTarget.why: The Antenna Genius has its own Ethernet port with a static IP on your Station LAN.
stationTarget.howToFind: Check the AG's display or use the Antenna Genius App to view its IP address. Set a static IP in the AG's network settings.
stationTarget.ifWrong: The Antenna Genius App will fail to connect. The AG's front panel still works locally.

clientNotes: Antenna Genius App -> Settings -> IP Address: 127.0.0.1, Port: 9007
N4PY: set Antenna Genius address to 127.0.0.1:9007
stationNotes: Antenna Genius must have a static IP on the Station LAN
Connect AG to your Station LAN switch via Ethernet cable
radioNotes: Physical: Connect Antenna Genius to LAN switch with standard Ethernet cable
Physical: Connect antenna coax cables to the AG's SO-239 ports
Physical: Power the AG with the included 12V power supply

stationTarget.label: Rotator Genius IP address on the Station's LAN
stationTarget.why: The Rotator Genius has its own Ethernet port with a static IP.
stationTarget.howToFind: Check the Rotator Genius display or app. Set a static IP in its network settings.
stationTarget.ifWrong: The Rotator Genius App will fail to connect.

clientNotes: Rotator Genius App -> Settings -> IP Address: 127.0.0.1, Port: 9006
stationNotes: Rotator Genius must have a static IP on the Station LAN
radioNotes: Physical: Connect Rotator Genius to LAN switch via Ethernet cable
Physical: Connect rotator motor cable to the Rotator Genius motor output
Physical: Connect rotator position feedback cable to the RG's sensor input

stationTarget.label: CAT2LAN IP address on the Station's LAN
stationTarget.why: The CAT2LAN bridges RS-232/CI-V serial to Ethernet. It has its own IP on your LAN.
stationTarget.howToFind: Use the CAT2LAN configuration software to view/set its IP address.
stationTarget.ifWrong: CAT commands will time out. Verify the CAT2LAN's IP hasn't changed (use static IP).

clientNotes: Configure your logging software to connect to 127.0.0.1:4001 for CAT control
The CAT2LAN appears as a TCP serial port -- your software connects over TCP instead of a COM port
stationNotes: CAT2LAN must have a static IP on the Station LAN
Configure the CAT2LAN's serial parameters to match your radio (baud, CI-V address, etc.)
radioNotes: Physical: Connect CAT2LAN to radio via RS-232 or CI-V cable
Physical: Connect CAT2LAN to Station LAN switch via Ethernet cable
Physical: Power via USB or included power adapter

stationTarget.label: ARCO IP address on the Station's LAN
stationTarget.why: The ARCO has a built-in Ethernet port and VNC server. You control it via a VNC viewer.
stationTarget.howToFind: Check ARCO's LAN settings menu on its touch screen, or use your router's DHCP client list.
stationTarget.ifWrong: VNC viewer will fail to connect. The ARCO's touch screen still works locally.

clientNotes: Open any VNC Viewer (TightVNC, RealVNC, etc.) and connect to 127.0.0.1:5900
You will see an exact replica of the ARCO's touch screen display
Full control of rotator, presets, relay modules, and settings via VNC
stationNotes: ARCO must have a static IP on the Station LAN (set via its Settings -> LAN menu)
radioNotes: Physical: Connect ARCO to LAN switch via Ethernet cable (100-BaseTX)
Physical: Connect rotator motor cable to ARCO's motor output terminals
Physical: Connect rotator feedback potentiometer to ARCO's sensor input
Physical: Power ARCO with the 48V switching power supply (motor) and 13.5V (logic)

stationTarget.label: KPA1500 IP address on the Station's LAN
stationTarget.why: The KPA1500 has a built-in Ethernet port. The Elecraft remote software connects to it directly.
stationTarget.howToFind: Check the KPA1500's UTIL menu -> ENET -> IP ADDR. Set a static IP.
stationTarget.ifWrong: Elecraft remote software will fail to connect. The amp's front panel still works.

clientNotes: Elecraft KPA Remote Software -> Connection -> IP: 127.0.0.1, Port: 4626
You get full amplifier control: power, band, tune, fault monitoring
stationNotes: KPA1500 must have a static IP on the Station LAN
Enable the Ethernet interface in UTIL -> ENET menu
radioNotes: Physical: Connect KPA1500 to LAN switch via Ethernet cable (rear panel RJ-45)
Physical: Standard RF connections to transceiver (ANT IN) and antenna (ANT OUT)
Physical: KEY/ALC/INHIBIT connections as per normal amplifier installation

forwards.name: KPA500-Serial
forwards.notes: KPA500 serial control via TCP bridge

stationTarget.label: Serial bridge target address
stationTarget.why: The KPA500 connects via USB (virtual COM port) to the Station PC. VSPE bridges it to TCP.
stationTarget.howToFind: 127.0.0.1 -- the serial bridge runs on the Station PC.
stationTarget.ifWrong: The serial bridge will fail to connect to the amplifier.

clientNotes: Elecraft KPA Remote Software connects to a virtual COM port (created by VSPE TcpClient)
Alternatively, some software can connect directly to TCP (127.0.0.1:<port>)
stationNotes: Install VSPE on the Station PC
Create a TcpServer device bridging the KPA500's USB COM port to TCP
Baud rate: 38400, 8N1 (KPA500 default)
radioNotes: Physical: Connect KPA500 to Station PC via USB cable (rear panel USB-B port)
Physical: The KPA500 appears as a virtual COM port (e.g. COM5) on the Station PC
Physical: Standard RF connections (ANT IN from transceiver, ANT OUT to antenna)

forwards.name: SPE-Remote
forwards.notes: SPE Expert amplifier remote control (via LAN-UNIT)

stationTarget.label: SPE LAN-UNIT IP address
stationTarget.why: The SPE LAN-UNIT is an Ethernet adapter that plugs into the amplifier's RS-232 port and provides TCP/IP access.
stationTarget.howToFind: Check the LAN-UNIT's configuration (default IP may be DHCP -- set a static IP).
stationTarget.ifWrong: SPE remote software will fail to connect.

clientNotes: SPE Remote Control software -> Connect to: 127.0.0.1, Port: 8888
Term_2K application also works via this TCP connection
stationNotes: SPE LAN-UNIT must be installed on the amplifier and connected to the Station LAN
Set a static IP address on the LAN-UNIT
radioNotes: Physical: Plug SPE LAN-UNIT into the amplifier's rear RS-232 port
Physical: Connect LAN-UNIT to Station LAN switch via Ethernet cable
Physical: Standard amplifier RF and control connections

forwards.name: SPE-Serial
forwards.notes: SPE Expert serial control via TCP bridge

stationTarget.label: Serial bridge target address
stationTarget.why: The SPE amplifier connects via RS-232 serial to the Station PC. VSPE bridges it to TCP.
stationTarget.howToFind: 127.0.0.1 -- the serial bridge runs on the Station PC.
stationTarget.ifWrong: The bridge will fail to reach the amplifier.

clientNotes: SPE Remote Control / Term_2K connects to a virtual COM port (VSPE TcpClient) or directly via TCP
stationNotes: Connect amplifier's RS-232 port to Station PC via serial cable (or USB-serial adapter)
Create VSPE TcpServer bridging that COM port to TCP
Baud rate: 9600, 8N1 (SPE default)
radioNotes: Physical: Connect SPE amplifier rear RS-232 port to Station PC via DB-9 serial cable
Physical: If Station PC has no serial port, use a USB-to-RS232 adapter
Physical: Standard amplifier RF and control connections (PTT, ALC, RF)

stationTarget.label: Serial bridge target address
stationTarget.why: The RT-21 connects via RS-232 to the Station PC. VSPE bridges it to TCP.
stationTarget.howToFind: 127.0.0.1 -- the serial bridge runs on the Station PC.
stationTarget.ifWrong: Rotator commands will time out.

clientNotes: Configure your rotator control software (PstRotator, N1MM, GHTracker) to use the virtual COM port
Protocol: GS-232A compatible (or use greenctld for hamlib compatibility)
Alternative: run greenctld on Station PC and forward its TCP port (4533) instead of raw serial
stationNotes: Connect RT-21's RS-232 port to Station PC via serial cable
VSPE TcpServer bridges the COM port to TCP
Baud rate: 4800, 8N1 (RT-21 default -- verify in RT-21 settings)
radioNotes: Physical: Connect RT-21 to Station PC via DB-9 RS-232 cable (rear panel 'COMPUTER' port)
Physical: RT-21 control cable to rotator motor/brake
Physical: Rotator feedback cable to RT-21 sensor input
Note: The RT-21 uses 4800 baud by default but this is configurable in its setup menu

stationTarget.label: Serial bridge target address
stationTarget.why: The OptimizIR connects via USB to the Station PC. VSPE bridges the virtual COM port to TCP.
stationTarget.howToFind: 127.0.0.1 -- the serial bridge runs on the Station PC.
stationTarget.ifWrong: SteppIR commands will time out.

clientNotes: Use the OptimizIR 'Remote Terminal' feature pointed at the virtual COM port
Or use custom software via the serial-over-TCP bridge
stationNotes: Connect OptimizIR to Station PC via USB cable
Note the COM port number assigned (Device Manager -> Ports)
VSPE TcpServer bridges that COM port to TCP
Baud rate: 9600, 8N1
radioNotes: Physical: Connect OptimizIR controller to Station PC via USB cable
Physical: Control cable from OptimizIR to antenna elements (as per SteppIR installation guide)
Physical: The OptimizIR requires 12V DC power

forwards.name: Alpha87A-Serial
forwards.notes: Alpha 87A RS-232 control via TCP bridge

stationTarget.label: Serial bridge target address
stationTarget.why: The Alpha 87A has an RS-232 port (DB-25) for computer control. VSPE bridges it to TCP.
stationTarget.howToFind: 127.0.0.1 -- the serial bridge runs on the Station PC.
stationTarget.ifWrong: Amplifier monitoring will not connect.

clientNotes: Configure your amplifier monitoring software to use the virtual COM port
N1MM+ and Logger32 can read Alpha 87A status via this connection
stationNotes: Connect Alpha 87A RS-232 port to Station PC via DB-25 to DB-9 serial cable
The 87A talks whenever plugged into mains power (even when off)
VSPE TcpServer bridges the COM port to TCP
Baud rate: 9600, 8N1 (set by jumpers on the 87A's DB-25 connector)
radioNotes: Physical: Connect Alpha 87A rear DB-25 RS-232 port to Station PC
Physical: You will need a DB-25 to DB-9 null-modem cable (or DB-25 to USB-serial adapter)
Physical: Baud rate is set by jumpering pins on the DB-25 connector (see Alpha 87A manual)
Physical: Default is 9600 baud -- verify jumper settings match

forwards.name: ACOM2000A-Serial
forwards.notes: ACOM 2000A serial control via TCP bridge

stationTarget.label: Serial bridge target address
stationTarget.why: The ACOM 2000A has an RS-232 serial interface for computer control. VSPE bridges it to TCP.
stationTarget.howToFind: 127.0.0.1 -- the serial bridge runs on the Station PC.
stationTarget.ifWrong: Amplifier control/monitoring will not connect.

clientNotes: Configure your amplifier control software to use the virtual COM port
The ACOM 2000A uses CI-V style protocol at 1200 baud
stationNotes: Connect ACOM 2000A RS-232 port to Station PC
VSPE TcpServer bridges the COM port to TCP
Baud rate: 1200, 8N1 (ACOM 2000A default -- very slow, do not change)
radioNotes: Physical: Connect ACOM 2000A rear RS-232 (DB-9) port to Station PC via serial cable
Physical: If Station PC has no serial port, use a USB-to-RS232 adapter
Physical: Baud rate is fixed at 1200 baud -- ensure VSPE is configured to match
Note: The official ACOM eBox (Ethernet adapter) is an alternative if you prefer no VSPE setup

entries.displayName: Web Power Switch (remote AC power control)

forwards.name: DLI-WebPower
forwards.notes: Digital Loggers Web Power Switch HTTP interface

stationTarget.label: Web Power Switch IP address on the Station's LAN
stationTarget.why: The Web Power Switch has its own Ethernet port with a static IP. You control the outlets via its built-in web page, which the Station forwards to you over the tunnel.
stationTarget.howToFind: Check the switch's LCD (if equipped) or your router's DHCP client list. Set a static IP in the switch's Setup -> Network page so the rule doesn't break on a lease change.
stationTarget.ifWrong: The forwarded web page will fail to load. The switch's outlets still work locally and via its front panel.

clientNotes: Open a web browser to http://127.0.0.1/ to reach the Web Power Switch control page
Bookmark it for one-click access to cycle station power (radio, amp, rotator, PC, etc.)
The REST/HTTP API also works through the tunnel for scripted power control
stationNotes: The Web Power Switch must have a static IP on the Station LAN

IMPORTANT: In the switch's Setup -> Security page, you MUST change the access setting so it is NOT limited to the local LAN. By default many Digital Loggers units restrict web access to same-subnet clients; because RWK forwards the connection from the Station's loopback, the switch may see it as a non-LAN request and refuse it. Disable 'Allow only local access' (or the equivalent LAN-restriction option) and set a strong admin password.
Set a strong username/password on the switch -- once forwarded, anyone with tunnel access can control station power
radioNotes: Physical: Connect the Web Power Switch to your Station LAN switch via Ethernet cable
Physical: Plug station equipment (radio, amplifier, rotator, PC) into the switched outlets
Physical: A power-cycle-able Station PC should NOT be plugged into a switched outlet you might turn off remotely -- keep it on an always-on outlet or you will lock yourself out

stationTarget.label: Serial bridge target address
stationTarget.why: The TCP serial server (VSPE TcpServer, com2tcp, or ser2net) listens on this address at the Station.
stationTarget.howToFind: 127.0.0.1 if the serial server runs on the Station PC itself.
stationTarget.ifWrong: The virtual COM port on the client will not connect.

basePort.label: TCP port for the serial bridge
basePort.why: Each serial device needs its own TCP port. Default starts at 4000 and increments.
basePort.howToFind: Use any available port. 4000 is a good default for the first device.
basePort.ifWrong: Port conflict -- another service may already be using that port.

clientNotes: Install VSPE or com0com on this PC
Create a TcpClient virtual COM port pointing at 127.0.0.1:<port>
Configure your logger to use the virtual COM port
stationNotes: Install VSPE or com2tcp on the Station PC
Create a TcpServer listening on 0.0.0.0:<port> connected to the real COM port
Match baud rate, data bits, parity, stop bits to the device

stationTarget.label: Service target address
stationTarget.why: Where does this service listen on the Station's network?
stationTarget.howToFind: 127.0.0.1 if it's on the Station PC. Otherwise, the device's LAN IP.
stationTarget.ifWrong: Connection will time out or be refused.

clientNotes: Connect your client software to 127.0.0.1:<port>
stationNotes: Ensure the target service is running and accessible

stationTarget.label: Service target address
stationTarget.why: Where does this service listen on the Station's network?
stationTarget.howToFind: 127.0.0.1 if it's on the Station PC. Otherwise, the device's LAN IP.
stationTarget.ifWrong: Datagrams will be sent but never arrive.

clientNotes: Send UDP datagrams to 127.0.0.1:<port>
stationNotes: Ensure the target service is listening on the specified port

stationTarget.label: Source address on the Station
stationTarget.why: Where does the Station-side application connect FROM? This is the address it will reach the tunnel on. Usually 127.0.0.1.
stationTarget.howToFind: 127.0.0.1 if the Station application connects to localhost.
stationTarget.ifWrong: The Station application won't reach the tunnel endpoint.

clientNotes: The Station-side service will appear on this PC at 127.0.0.1:<port>
Configure your Client-side software to listen on or connect to that address
stationNotes: The Station-side application connects to 127.0.0.1:<port> -- traffic is tunneled to the Client

stationTarget.label: Source address on the Station
stationTarget.why: Where does the Station-side application send UDP datagrams FROM? Usually 127.0.0.1.
stationTarget.howToFind: 127.0.0.1 if the application runs on the Station PC itself.
stationTarget.ifWrong: Datagrams from the Station won't reach the tunnel.

clientNotes: UDP datagrams from the Station will arrive at 127.0.0.1:<port> on this PC
Configure your Client-side software to listen on that port
stationNotes: The Station-side application sends UDP to 127.0.0.1:<port> -- traffic is tunneled to the Client
